checkpointRows.reviewNotes: The teaching-hall referent is concrete, but documentary narrators and a ceremony speaker are stored as MasterName. Building narration and imperial-occasion directions require non-master/narrated attribution, not linked masters.

The Zilu citation-life is appropriately narrow, but quotation ownership is not demonstrated: named Chan speakers may quote a Confucian line whose embedded utterer differs. Full-case actor notes must distinguish quoter from quoted figure.

The verbal-material definition is strong, but Fada and Jiangxi Zhiche may be discussed figures or questioners rather than exact utterers. Eight universally named rows need turn-by-turn proof, especially inherited quotations.

The public-theme act is plausible, but 'raise the theme' as action and a book/section heading are different grammatical owners. The all-named attribution pattern needs narration and request turns separated from the master performing 提綱.

The bathing rite and anti-symbolism boundary are strong, but Dogen is forbidden/out of Chinese-Chan scope and cannot be a MasterName or source authority here. That contamination alone requires replacement; ceremony actors also need exact review.

The emergence action is useful, but two documentary-narrator labels and a compiler label occupy MasterName. Narrated cases and quoted Linji positions must be attributed to exact utterers, not database role strings.

The institutional sacred-monk image is clearly pictured, but compiler and ceremony-speaker labels are MasterName. Rules assigning the image a seat are narration; Danxia may act on or mention the image without owning every stored clause.

The heat-and-cold question is accurately bounded, but the later commemoration speaker is a syntax label, not a roster master. Jiashan's original questioner versus answerer and Yuanwu's later citation need distinct exact actors.

The literal skull and speech bend are strong, but ceremony-speaker and Shakyamuni rows require quoted/narrative ownership review. A person appearing in the skull story is not automatically the utterer of the headword-bearing narration.

The grouped audience definition is useful, but inscription author and assembly speaker are non-master role labels in MasterName. Documentary inscription language requires identified author/narration, not fabricated master links.
